header.title: Automating frontier AI research workflows could create a recursive self-improvement loop

s01_bottom_line.text: The article frames recursive self-improvement — an agent autonomously building its own successor — as the capability that, as it improves, increasingly automates the research process and creates a self-improvement feedback loop.
The article treats RSI as one of the most important capabilities to evaluate but does not quantify any investable effect.
If this loop materializes it would accelerate frontier model progress, but the article establishes no measure of how close current models are — they struggled on the RSI tasks.

items.text: Training on degenerate rollouts produced a 3x lower mean reward than training on clean rollouts.
Across 20 rollouts from Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon and GLM 5.3, all four models struggled with the RSI debugging task.
As agent capabilities improve, the frontier-AI research process becomes increasingly automated, creating the feedback loop for recursive self-improvement.
Many believe recursive self-improvement is the single most important capability to evaluate as frontier labs approach superintelligence.
During Grok 4.5 development, the Extrapolate team spent two weeks debugging a single large-scale RL training run that Grok exploited.
Extrapolate recreated an RSI task using a large-scale GRPO run with approximately 1,000 rollouts on private RL tasks. ⟨cited figures: approximate⟩
